title: Agent written with the functional API streams no model tokens
summary: When the same assistant is written with the functional API instead of the graph builder, streaming messages yields one complete model message at the end and no token chunks. The graph-builder version of the same agent streams token by token as expected.
expected: Token chunks arrive while the model is generating, whichever API defines the agent.
actual: The functional version emits a single finished message with no chunks.
fixReasoning: A model call made inside a task is filed under its caller's checkpoint namespace even though it runs in the caller's own graph. The streaming handlers only stripped the final namespace segment, so such a call looked like it belonged to a subgraph, and its events were discarded unless subgraph streaming was switched on. The fix makes the handlers also remove one segment for every enclosing task call, using the path the task records, so model and tool events from tasks carry the namespace of the graph that ran them.
fixChange: Message and tool stream handlers now skip one namespace segment per enclosing task call, based on the task's recorded path, so events raised in tasks are attributed to their own graph. Related rules were tightened for graphs that run outside the caller's task and for pushed messages.

title: Forcing a function tool that is named like a hosted tool selects the hosted tool
summary: On the Responses API an agent can carry its own function tool with a name that matches a hosted tool type, for example web_search. Setting the tool choice to that name makes the SDK send a hosted-tool selector rather than a function selector, although only the function was advertised, so the caller's own tool cannot be forced.
expected: The request selects the local function by name whenever such a function or handoff is configured.
actual: The request carries a selector for a hosted tool that was never in the tools list, and it fails with an HTTP 400 error.
fixReasoning: The converter turned certain tool-choice strings into hosted-tool selectors before it considered local functions, and it never checked which tools were actually advertised. A name shared by a function and a hosted tool was therefore resolved the wrong way. The fix resolves the choice against the advertised tool list and lets the hosted tool win only when it is really present.
fixChange: Resolve the tool choice against the tools sent in the request, on both the native and the any-llm Responses paths: a function or handoff with a matching name is selected as a function, and the hosted tool wins only if it is also configured.

title: Parallel tool calls on one streamable HTTP MCP server run one after another
summary: With the streamable HTTP MCP client, every request to a single server waits on a shared lock. Several tool calls requested together, or several runs sharing one connected server, queue up instead of overlapping, so four calls of three seconds each take about twelve seconds instead of about three.
expected: Independent requests on one session overlap, as they do over the stdio transport.
actual: Requests are handled strictly one at a time, and total time grows with the number of parallel calls.
fixReasoning: The per-session lock was added when an older version of the MCP library let one failed POST on the shared transport cancel its siblings. On the newer major version an HTTP error fails only its own request, so nothing was left for the lock to protect and it only cost throughput. Keeping it for the old version and dropping it for the new one preserves safety where it still matters.
fixChange: Serialize session requests only when running on MCP v1; on MCP v2 let independent requests overlap. Document the retry trade-off: after a dropped connection, tools that were already in flight may have taken effect, and retrying could run them twice.

title: Wrapping a callback parameter in Annotated breaks tool schema generation
summary: Creating a tool from a function, or from a component, normally leaves callable parameters out of the schema shown to the model. When such a callback parameter carries extra metadata through typing's Annotated wrapper, the detector no longer recognises it as a callable, and schema creation fails with an error.
expected: The callback stays out of the schema exactly as it does without the wrapper, and calling the tool still uses the callback's default.
actual: Tool creation raises a schema generation error because a JSON schema cannot be produced for a callable.
fixReasoning: The check that decides whether a parameter is a callable inspected the annotation directly, so the Annotated wrapper hid the real type. Plain callbacks were skipped, but wrapped ones reached the JSON schema builder and failed. Looking through the wrapper gives both the same treatment.
fixChange: Make the shared callable detector unwrap Annotated before testing the parameter type, which covers tool creation from functions and from components, including optional callbacks on either side of the wrapper. Add regression tests and a release note.

title: Tool serialization error prints a literal placeholder instead of the cause
summary: When pickle-based serialization of a tool fails, the raised error says the object cannot be serialized and then shows a literal placeholder instead of the underlying exception. Another error path in the same module formats the same message correctly.
expected: The error text includes the actual exception details, which helps diagnose the failure.
actual: The message ends with the variable name in braces, so the real cause is hidden.
fixReasoning: The format string escaped its braces by doubling them, which makes Python print them as they are instead of substituting the variable. A single pair of braces substitutes the exception, as the sibling error path in the same file already did.
fixChange: Replace the doubled braces with a single pair in the serialization error message so the caught exception is interpolated into the text.
